g12-biology-ub6-t1.overview: Climate change is the greenhouse effect working overtime: since industrialization, human activity — burning fossil fuels, cement-making, deforestation and farming — has thickened the atmosphere's heat-trapping blanket, and global mean temperature has already risen ~1.2-1.3 °C above pre-industrial. This topic establishes the physics (radiation balance, the greenhouse gases and their potencies), the evidence (temperature, ice-core CO₂ records, sea level, phenology), and Ethiopia's paradox: among the smallest emitters per person, among the most exposed.
objectives: Explain Earth's energy balance and the natural greenhouse effect
Rank the greenhouse gases by emission and potency (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, F-gases)
Read the evidence: ice cores, thermometers, satellites, sea level
Identify the human sources: energy, industry, land use, agriculture
Estimate Ethiopia's contribution and vulnerability profile
g12-biology-ub6-t1.simple: The planet wears a blanket; we made it thicker. Sunlight (shortwave) passes the atmosphere, warms the surface, and Earth re-emits infrared — which greenhouse gases absorb and re-radiate downward: naturally +33 °C of warmth (−18 °C without it: a frozen rock). The enhanced effect: CO₂ from coal, oil and gas plus cement (~75% of emissions), methane CH₄ from agriculture, landfills and gas leaks (80× CO₂'s 20-year punch), nitrous oxide N₂O from fertilizers (Unit 2's nitrifiers exhaling it), and the fluorinated industrial gases. Proof of human ownership: ice cores show CO₂ held 180-300 ppm for 800 000 years and sits at ~424 today; the emitted carbon's isotopic fingerprint (fossil C carries no ¹⁴C) and falling ¹³C ratio point at fossil sources; and the stratosphere COOLS while the surface warms — the greenhouse signature, not solar. Ethiopia emits ~0.15 t CO₂/person/yr (global average ~4.7) yet faces rainfall shift, glacier-loss (the last Simien ice vanished), and recurrent drought — the injustice that frames Unit 6.
g12-biology-ub6-t1.detailed:
Energy budget. Earth intercepts ~1 200 W/m² average, reflects ~30% (albedo: ice bright, forest dark — the feedback: melting exposes dark ocean that absorbs more heat, accelerating the melt: the Arctic amplification; deforestation's local version: bare highland soil changes heat and water fluxes). The remaining absorbed radiation balances emission to space; the atmosphere's opaque IR bands (CO₂'s 15 µm, H₂O's rotation band, CH₄, N₂O, O₃) mean emission to space comes from colder heights — the surface must warm to push the same energy out: the greenhouse effect in one sentence. Radiative forcing since 1750: ~+2.7 W/m² total (CO₂ ~+2.1, CH₄ ~+0.5, others less) — small number, enormous consequence: per degree of warming the climate system's heat content climbs by a vast ocean-heat tally (~93% of the extra energy went to the oceans: the 'global warming is ocean heating' frame). Feedbacks decide the sensitivity: water vapor (amplifies: warmer air holds ~7% more vapor per °C — itself a greenhouse gas), ice-albedo (amplifies), clouds (the big uncertainty: which altitude, which type), carbon-cycle sinks (dampen now, may weaken: the t3 warning about the land sink faltering).

The gases, one by one. CO₂: not the most potent but the most NUMEROUS and longest-lived (centuries: the cumulative-emissions logic — every future ton matters because the budget is a stock problem, not a rate problem); fossil fuel and industry dominate, land-use change second. CH₄: 25-30× CO₂ over a century (80× over 20 — the near-term lever: cutting methane buys fast cooling: livestock, rice, landfills, gas-leak repair); its atmospheric lifetime ~12 years (oxidized by OH radicals — Unit 2's microbial methanotrophs eat some too). N₂O: from nitrogen fertilizer and manure — the microbial nitrification/denitrification of t2's soil chapter now amplified by global nitrogen application; ~270× CO₂ and also the chief ozone-destroyer of today. F-gases (refrigerants): tiny volumes, enormous potency, the Montreal-to-Kigali regulatory thread (the ozone protocol's HFC substitute turned out itself to be a greenhouse gas — the Kigali amendment phases it down: a lesson in policy second-best). And the 'black carbon' aerosols (cooking fires, diesel: darkening snow, warming regionally — the clean-cookstove intervention is ALSO climate action: Unit 2's indoor air and Unit 6's forcing meet).

The evidence stack (what a skeptic must explain away). Instrumental: ten warmest years on record all since 2014; warming ~0.2 °C/decade accelerating. Palaeo: ice-core CO₂-temperature lockstep over 800 kyr with today's CO₂ beyond any glacial-interglacial range; tree rings, corals, sediments reconstructing the past two millennia's unusual heat. Physical: Arctic sea-ice minimum shrinking ~13%/decade; glaciers retreating worldwide (the Simien's seasonal ice gone — the Rwenzori next door lost 90% since 1906); Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets losing mass (satellite gravimetry); sea level up ~20 cm since 1900 and accelerating (thermal expansion + meltwater: the low-lying delta nations' existential arithmetic). Biological — the fingerprint biology can see: phenology shifts (flowering and bird migration earlier by days/decade everywhere measured), species' ranges moving poleward and UPWARD (montane species squeezed toward summits — Ethiopia's endemic highland frogs and the Simien fox's habitat edges), and Ocean: acidification (t3's chemical invoice). The converging pattern — warming troposphere + cooling stratosphere + isotopic fossil signature + asymmetric day-night and seasonal warming — has exactly one explanation that fits ALL of it: greenhouse forcing from human emissions.

Ethiopia's profile. Contribution: ~0.15 t CO₂e/person vs global 4.7, total ~0.1% of cumulative emissions — with energy nearly all renewable (the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam: 6+ GW hydro as the grid's backbone, geothermal potential in the Afar's volcanics — the very rift-volcanism that dated Lucy is now the clean-power resource, and wind at Ashegoda and Adama). Exposure: the Sahel-rainfall belt's variability (the 1983-85 and 2015-16 droughts' tens of millions in need; the Indian-Ocean dipole's modulation of the kiremt rains), the drylands' 80%-of-population rainfall dependence, and the land-restoration frontier (the exclosures and terracing of Units 1 and 3 as carbon AND resilience work). Ethiopia's declared stance at every climate summit: adaptation first (the CRGE since 2011, now the Climate Resilient Green Economy → the ten-year development plan with its green-legacy line), finance and technology transfer as the justice claim, and net-ZERO-by-2050 promised — a developing country's pledge whose emissions would rise with development: 'we will grow out of poverty without the carbon ladder you climbed' — the whole negotiation philosophy of Unit 6 compressed into one sentence.

workedExamples.problem: Why does the stratosphere cooling FALSIFY the 'sun got stronger' hypothesis?
workedExamples.calculation: More solar input would warm ALL layers; greenhouse trapping warms surface while the upper layer radiates to a thinner IR blanket.
workedExamples.answer: The cooling aloft is the fingerprint of trapped heat below — one of the cleanest discriminations in the data.

workedExamples.problem: Fossil fuels are millions of years old: what isotope signature do they carry?
workedExamples.calculation: ¹⁴C has decayed away (half-life 5 730 yr: after a few Myr, zero).
workedExamples.answer: Emitted CO₂ is ¹⁴C-dead — measured in air: the carbon is demonstrably fossil, i.e. ours.

workedExamples.problem: Cutting methane vs cutting CO₂: which cools faster?
workedExamples.calculation: CH₄ lifetime ~12 yr vs CO₂'s centuries: reducing CH₄ drops forcing within years.
workedExamples.answer: Methane is the near-term throttle and CO₂ the long debt: you need both, and the physics says methane first for speed.

workedExamples.problem: Ethiopia's per-capita emissions vs the USA's, roughly?
workedExamples.answer: A factor of ~100: the exposure-to-contribution gap IS the climate-justice argument.

commonMistakes: 'The greenhouse effect is the problem' (the ENHANCED effect is; the natural one is why we exist)
Confusing ozone depletion with climate change (twin but distinct: CFCs were both)
Thinking CO₂ is the most potent gas (it's the most important by quantity and persistence)
Weather = climate (a single drought 'proving' or 'disproving' trends: statistics, not anecdotes)
Believing the debate is about the basic physics (it is about magnitude, timing and who pays)
applications: GERD and geothermal: the rift's own clean-energy endowment
Clean cookstoves: black carbon and indoor health cut together
Cattle-feed and landfill methane: the fast-lever programs
Ethiopia's CRGE and net-zero-by-2050 pledge as development strategy
g12-biology-ub6-t1.summary: Thicker greenhouse blankets from fossil CO₂, agricultural methane, fertilizer nitrous oxide and industry's gases are warming the planet ~1.2 °C with fingerprints (isotopes, cooling stratosphere, biology) that rule out natural causes — and Ethiopia, a ~0.1%-cumulative emitter, carries top-tier exposure.

g12-biology-ub6-t2.overview: Climate change's effects run through every living system: crops and livestock, water and forests, disease vectors and coasts, biodiversity and the human body itself. This topic tours the impact cascade — physical → ecological → human — with Ethiopia as the case study: shifting kiremt rains, the spread of malaria up the highlands, the maize-and-coffee futures, rangeland pressure, and the adaptation toolbox (drought-tolerant seed, water harvesting, early warning, climate-smart agriculture).
objectives: Trace physical impacts: temperature, rainfall, extremes, sea level
Explain ecological impacts: ranges, phenology, coral, forests
Assess agricultural impacts: yields, livestock, coffee, teff
Describe health impacts: heat, malaria, malnutrition, water disease
List adaptation strategies and Ethiopia's programs
g12-biology-ub6-t2.simple: Warmth is the insult; everything else is the response. Physical: heat waves longer, rainfall more erratic (wet places wetter, dry places drier on average — plus the killers: the 2022 Horn drought's four failed rainy seasons, and floods like the 2006 Borana or 2020 Awash outbreaks), sea level rising toward deltas and islands. Ecological: species move poleward and uphill (mountaintop species have nowhere left); corals bleach (the Great Barrier's repeated mass events); flowering and migration desynchronize (puffins missing chickling, caterpillars ahead of tits — the phenological mismatch). Agricultural: every ~1 °C without adaptation costs staple yields ~3-10%; Ethiopia's teff, maize, wheat face rain-shift; coffee (a highland shade crop) loses suitable ground to warming (the 'coffee belt' climbing and shrinking — genetic rescue from wild forests, Unit 4's library again). Health: heat stroke (Unit 5's loop saturated), malaria climbing into formerly cold highlands (the vector's temperature ceiling moves up the slopes — Ethiopia's highland epidemics of the 1990s-2000s are the documented case), cholera after floods, undernutrition from failed harvests (the stunting arithmetic). Adaptation: drought-tolerant varieties, soil-water conservation, irrigation, weather-index insurance, early-warning and anticipatory cash (Ethiopia's PSNP + forecast-based financing), protected areas as species corridors.
g12-biology-ub6-t2.detailed:
Physical layer. Mean warming is the headline but EXTREMES do the damage: heat waves (the 2003 Europe mortality of ~70 000 as the textbook — a developed continent shocked by a percentile event), heavy-rain intensification (~7% more vapor per °C: the same storms dumping more water: Addis' condominium-era flash floods and the 2024 Gulf floods), drought duration (soil moisture feedbacks: dry soil heats and dries further — the flash-drought mechanism that made the Horn's consecutive failed seasons a famine risk four times running: 2020-2023). Glaciers and water towers: the tropical glaciers (Simien seasonal remnants gone, Kilimanjaro's ice ~85% lost since 1912, Andean glaciers feeding cities) — the arithmetic of dry seasons with no storage; sea level: the 20 cm already risen + committed rise (thermal expansion inertia and ice-sheet lag: the ~0.5-1 m by 2100 under medium paths — Bangladesh's delta, the Pacific atolls, and Egypt's Nile mouth on the vulnerable list; Africa's coastlines mostly UNLOCK their exposure only through poverty, not geography).

Ecological layer. Range shifts measured globally (~17 km poleward and ~11 m upward per decade average for terrestrial species — the rate is now faster than many species' natural dispersal, so losers exist: the endemic montane taxa, the afroalpine specialists whose mountains are islands — Ethiopia's endemic frogs and the Simien fox's highland grasslands — squeeze to extinction first). Phenological mismatch: the hatching-chick/caterpillar peak desynchronization (the European pied flycatcher's decline as a documented casualty), and crop-pollinator timing (Unit 1's bees). Ecosystem phase shifts: coral bleaching (zooxanthellae expelled at +1-2 °C sustained; repeated events prevent recovery — reefs are the rainforests of the sea and 50% already lost), savanna-forest boundaries moving with rainfall lines (the Sahel's greening/browning debate is exactly this), and mountain treelines creeping up. Tipping elements (the honest frontier): the Amazon's dieback edge, the Atlantic circulation's slowdown, boreal carbon release from thawing permafrost — the risks that transform a smooth problem into a staircase of thresholds; the permafrost is Unit 2's archaea waking to eat an ice-age carbon vault (the methane feedback nobody can un-thaw).

Agricultural layer — Ethiopia's account. Crops: teff (moisture-sensitive at flowering; rainfall shift lengthens the 'false starts' that waste seed — the smallholder's annual gamble), maize (heat at pollination kills set; the C4 advantage narrows past ~35 °C), wheat (the rust-and-rain calculus — heat stress plus the wheat rust's own northward march: Unit 2's pathogen on the move), coffee (the premium arabica needs 18-22 °C and distinct dry season; modeled suitable area in Ethiopia contracting ~40-60% by mid-century under medium scenarios UNLESS adaptation climbs — shade, higher sites, the wild genetic library of t4). Livestock: heat stress cuts milk and fertility (the Borana herd's water-point stress during drought: the 2020-23 losses in cattle and camel calves), forage and rangeland carrying capacity shrinking at the dry-season edges, and the human-livestock conflict lines that move the disease map (Unit 2's anthrax and rabies at the margins). Fisheries: Lake Tana's water level and temperature (the Labeobarbus flock's habitat — Unit 4's radiation facing a physics problem), and the ocean's tropicalization hitting the Red Sea's coral and fisheries. The adaptation menu at home: improved varieties (the EIAR's drought-tolerant maize and wheat lines, the teff 'durio' lodging fixes), soil-water conservation (the exclosures' terracing and the pond/haftom schemes), small-scale irrigation and solar pumps, weather-index livestock insurance (the RUSI pilots), anticipatory cash before the fourth failed rain (the PSNP's forecast-triggered scaling — the world's largest example of the instrument), and climate-informed extension (the meteorological service's agro-advisories reaching farmers by radio and mobile).

Human layer. Direct: heat illness and death (outdoor workers, the very old — Unit 5's loop saturated; Europe and South Asia's stadium of dead in each wave), flood drowning and displacement. Vector-borne: malaria's altitude frontier (the highlands held near-zero because Anopheles' development and parasite cycling had temperature ceilings — warming pushed transmission to towns that never carried it: the 1999-2001 Ethiopian highland epidemics are in the textbooks as a climate-sensitive event; further warming threatens Addis' own altitude edge — though urbanization and drainage pull the other way), dengue's arrival (the 2023-24 outbreak seasons in Dire Dawa and the Harar line: the vector Aedes aegypti finding new highland niches), and the Indian-Ocean dipole's modulating the Rift Valley fever's epizootics (the livestock-and-human cycle of t7 again). Food-mediated: undernutrition's stunting burden rising with each failed season (the intergenerational cost — child growth is the thermometer of climate). Water and conflict: the drylands' herd-farm boundary friction (the resource-conflict lens — where climate is a threat-multiplier rather than a gun), migration (rural-to-urban climate drift — Addis' growth partly an adaptation strategy of families), and the mental-health toll of lost harvests. Gender's line: water- and fuel-carrying falls on women and girls — every dried spring buys back an education day (the SDG ledger). The justice frame closes: the people least responsible, with the least adaptive capital (a Dutch farmer can buy irrigation; a Borana herder cannot buy a rainy season) — which is why Unit 6 ends with the conventions of t3: adaptation finance, loss-and-damage, and the Paris temperature limit as the defense of the vulnerable.

workedExamples.problem: A village's reliable spring fails in a longer dry season. Which impact layer is this?
workedExamples.calculation: Physical (rainfall/recharge) → ecological (vegetation) → livelihood (herding radius) → health (water disease).
workedExamples.answer: All four at once: the cascade is the definition of climate impact.

workedExamples.problem: Why did the 1990s highland malaria epidemics hit populations with NO immunity?
workedExamples.calculation: Warming crossed the vector's altitude ceiling into cold zones; the people had no ancestral exposure.
workedExamples.answer: Climate moved the disease line; immunology did the rest — a two-unit answer.

workedExamples.problem: Coffee suitable area in Ethiopia contracts; what is the genetic rescue path?
workedExamples.calculation: Wild forest populations + other species hold heat/drought alleles; breeding introgresses them.
workedExamples.answer: Unit 4's library is Unit 6's pharmacy: conserve the forests, breed the crop.

workedExamples.problem: Cash transfers arrive BEFORE the fourth failed rain (2023 pilot). Why is timing worth more than size?
workedExamples.calculation: Pre-emptive purchase of feed/water keeps the herd (and the family's capital) vs post-disaster salvage of starving animals.
workedExamples.answer: Anticipatory action converts catastrophe into expense: the herd survives the drought.

commonMistakes: Judging impacts by annual means (extremes and timing do the damage)
'Climate change just means warmer' (wet gets wetter, dry drier, seasons desynchronize)
Malaria spreading 'because mosquitoes like heat' (the precise thermal limits AND the immunity gap matter)
Treating adaptation as just technology (early warning, insurance, tenure and markets are the hard parts)
Assuming Africa's coast suffers most from geography (exposure is geography; loss is poverty)
applications: PSNP + forecast-based financing: the world's anticipatory-action flagship
EIAR drought-tolerant seed deployment across the woredas
Highland malaria early-warning and IRS expansion with warming fronts
Coffee genetic conservation in the Baale and Harenna forests
g12-biology-ub6-t2.summary: Warming cascades: extremes hit water and crops, species and seasons desynchronize, corals and highland disease lines move, and people pay in heat, hunger and displacement — while Ethiopia's adaptation toolkit (seed, water, insurance, early warning) is becoming a global model of the same cascade managed.

g12-biology-ub6-t3.overview: The climate convention story is humanity's attempt to run a global homeostatic loop on itself: the UNFCCC (1992) framed the problem, the Kyoto Protocol (1997) put binding numbers on the rich, Paris (2015) rewired the architecture to universal pledges with a 1.5-2 °C goal, and COP28 (2023) named the fossil era's end. This topic follows the negotiations, the mechanisms (finance, adaptation, loss-and-damage, carbon markets), and Ethiopia's negotiating line: green growth at home, justice abroad.
objectives: State the UNFCCC's objective and principle (CBDR)
Explain the 1.5-2 °C goal and the NDC mechanism
Describe climate finance, adaptation and loss-and-damage
Summarise Ethiopia's positions and domestic action
g12-biology-ub6-t3.simple: Three treaties, one planet. 1992 Rio — UNFCCC: stabilize greenhouse gases at levels preventing dangerous human interference; principle: common but differentiated responsibilities (everyone is in it, the rich started it and pay first). 1997 Kyoto — binding cuts for developed countries ONLY (the Annex-B numbers: the US signed but never ratified, Canada later withdrew: architecture flaw #1). 2015 Paris — universal but voluntary: every nation files its own pledge (Nationally Determined Contribution), updated every five years in one-way ratchets, with the temperature goal: hold well below 2 °C, pursue 1.5. The math that drives it: cumulative CO₂ budget — ~250-500 Gt CO₂ left for a 50% chance at 1.5 °C (at ~40 Gt/yr: 6-12 years of current pace), so 'net zero by 2050' is not a slogan, it is the budget's deadline. Money: the $100 billion/yr promise (late and under-delivered — trust deficit), the Green Climate Fund, the 2022 agreement of a Loss & Damage fund (Sharm el-Sheikh: the South's hardest ask, finally on the table), and adaptation finance stuck near ~7% of climate money while the vulnerable need half. Ethiopia's line: implement your pledges, honor the 1.5, and finance adaptation — while doing its own CRGE, the 15-billion-seedling campaign and net-zero-by-2050, and pushing for African renewable industrialization.
g12-biology-ub6-t3.detailed:
The architecture, evolutionarily. Why 1992's framework survived where politics died: it set a vague objective and left numbers to later protocols — the classic 'convene first, quantify later'. Kyoto (1997): top-down binding targets for industrialized nations, averaging 5% below 1990; its market mechanisms (emissions trading, Clean Development Mechanism: a rich country funding a poor-country project for credits) invented carbon pricing's tools but leaked emissions and excluded the growing South. Copenhagen 2009's near-collapse birthed the voluntary-pledge idea. Paris 2015: bottom-up universality — every country submits an NDC, a transparency framework verifies reporting, a global stocktake every 5 years compares to goals, and the ratchet expects pledges to only strengthen. Its weakness is Paris's strength: no enforcement, but no free-riding excuse either — and every 1.5 °C-relevant report since (the 2018 IPCC special report: 1.5 vs 2 °C differs by meters of sea, reefs, and hundreds of millions of poor) is aimed at the NDCs' combined gap (the 'emissions gap' report: current pledges leave us ~2.5-2.9 °C: the pledges ARE the policy). The finance leg: the $100bn/yr by 2020 promise (met — years late, ~$100-130bn in 2022 by broad counting — the concession-loan vs grant argument rages because a loan to a flood victim is not solidarity in practice), the New Collective Quantified Goal from 2025 (the Baku road-map toward a larger figure — the quantified justice debate ongoing), and the adaptation-finance sub-goal debate (money that keeps people alive rarely earns interest, so it is the least popular climate spending among donors). Loss and damage: the 30-year ask of the small-island and African groups (the 'we cannot adapt past a drowned home' case) conceded in principle at COP27 (2022, Sharm — hosted on a continent), operationalized at COP28 with a fund (the pledge total in hundreds of millions vs the losses in hundreds of billions: the scale gap is the next negotiation's fuel). Carbon markets: Paris Article 6 (trading credits between countries with 'corresponding adjustments' — the double-counting guard) and the voluntary offset market's integrity crisis (a 2023-24 forest-credit scandal wave: credits sold for avoided deforestation that never happened: the 'phantom offsets' cleanup — the economics of trust, once more).

The science-policy interface. The IPCC: 195 governments, thousands of scientists, assessment reports every ~6-8 years and special reports on request — its summary-for-policymakers lines are negotiated WORD BY WORD with governments present (the 'unequivocal' of 2021 arriving only in AR6: the consensus bottleneck explained — and why the report is slow but un-arguable once out). The 2018 1.5 °C report's shock: it quantified the remaining budget and made 'net zero by mid-century' standard policy language; the 2022 AR6's verdict: the window is narrow and closing, and its 'climate-resilient development' frame (mitigation + adaptation + development as one act, never sequential) is exactly Ethiopia's CRGE logic. The science that keeps the 1.5 alive: every fraction of a degree avoided pays back in reefs, meters of coast, heat-deaths and yield-loss — and the economic reversal by 2024: solar and wind now CHEAPER than coal and gas in most markets (the policy debate moved from cost to speed and justice).

Ethiopia at the table and at home. The African Group's shared asks (finance as grant not loan, adaptation parity, technology transfer, 1.5 honored) with Ethiopia as a big-seat voice, the ANC's chairman history, and the country's own record it cites when the West asks it to do more (the 2011-2024 CRGE: 70%+ of its NDC's ambitions conditional on finance it mostly hasn't received — the credibility of conditionality: the negotiating grievance made arithmetic; and yet the domestic story: 15 billion seedlings, the exclosures, 51% of energy from hydro and the GERD's export revenue, geothermal and wind build-out, and the industrial parks' green-power siting). The youth-and-science voice (the Fridays-for-Climat-Ethiopia chapters, the African Climate Academy, the university climate-science programs whose drought-attribution work gives the negotiating line a bibliography). The convention topic ends where all three units converge: biology supplies the evidence (Unit 3's cycles), the impacts (Unit 6's people), and the hope (the sinks, the crops, the forests) — and the negotiation is the species' feedback loop: the slowest thermostat ever built, but the only one the species owns.

keyTerms.def: 1997: binding cuts for the rich only

formulas.name: Carbon budget

workedExamples.problem: Why is 'net zero by 2050' arithmetically derived, not chosen?
workedExamples.calculation: Cumulative CO₂ sets peak temperature; 1.5 °C's budget ÷ current pace = exhaustion in ~6-12 yr; net-zero before exhaustion.
workedExamples.answer: The physics writes the deadline; the calendar only rounds it.

workedExamples.problem: A flood-hit country receives its 'climate finance' as a loan. The grievance?
workedExamples.calculation: It must repay the cost of a disaster it did not cause; debt service crowds out adaptation.
workedExamples.answer: Grant vs loan is the whole justice argument in one accounting line.

workedExamples.problem: A forest-offset project claims 'we stopped the chainsaws'. The integrity test?
workedExamples.calculation: Counterfactual: would deforestation in fact have happened at that site without the project?
workedExamples.answer: Exaggerated baselines: phantom offsets — credits must measure REAL avoided harm.

workedExamples.problem: Ethiopia's NDC: large fraction conditional on foreign finance. What does that signal?
workedExamples.calculation: CBDR in practice: ambition proportional to received support.
workedExamples.answer: The finance delivered vs promised IS the implementation gap's size.

commonMistakes: Confusing UNFCCC/Kyoto/Paris as one document (a tree of treaties and rules)
Thinking Paris has enforcement (it has transparency and ratchets, not penalties)
'Net zero' = zero emissions (it is balance: cuts to near zero + removals for the residue)
Reading the $100bn promise as met and sufficient (late, mixed quality, and far below adaptation need)
Believing the IPCC is an activist body (it is government-negotiated consensus: the slowness is the design)
applications: Ethiopia's CRGE + net-zero-by-2050 as the national submission record
The Green Climate Fund and adaptation projects in Ethiopian woredas
Loss & Damage fund: the Horn droughts as the case file
Article 6 readiness: Ethiopia's first bilateral carbon-cooperation agreements
g12-biology-ub6-t3.summary: Rio framed it, Kyoto tried top-down, Paris switched to universal ratcheting pledges under a 1.5-2 °C ceiling with finance, transparency and a loss-and-damage fund — while the carbon budget sets the 2050 deadline and Ethiopia negotiates adaptation justice against its own greening record.
